name: Energy
title: Renewable asset maintenance planning
summary: Combine turbine condition evidence, weather windows, and spare-part availability into engineer-approved maintenance plans.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A wind-farm operator receives vibration anomalies from several turbines before a forecast weather change. Maintenance planners must decide which inspections are feasible given crew skills, access restrictions, parts, and production commitments. Agents support planning; turbine protection and dispatch control remain outside their authority.
problem: An anomaly score is not a diagnosis, and forecast confidence changes with lead time. Recommending work from stale weather or incomplete maintenance history can waste a crew mobilization or introduce unsafe access assumptions.
whyAgents: Condition, history, weather, and resource specialists gather independent evidence. A validated scheduling service applies access and crew constraints; engineers evaluate hypotheses and approve work scope through the maintenance system.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Measure planning effort and evidence completeness before claiming availability improvements. Actual reliability depends on engineering diagnosis, field execution, and equipment behavior; retain those factors separately in the operational record.

agents.name: Condition evidence agent
agents.responsibility: Summarize vibration and temperature patterns with sensor quality and baseline context.
agents.boundary: Cannot change turbine control or declare equipment safe.

agents.name: Maintenance historian
agents.responsibility: Retrieve prior failures, component replacements, and open inspections.
agents.boundary: Cannot close inspections or infer repair completion.

agents.name: Access-window analyst
agents.responsibility: Compare forecast intervals with approved site access constraints.
agents.boundary: Cannot waive safety limits or authorize crew access.

agents.name: Resource planner
agents.responsibility: Draft work packages matching parts, skills, vessel or vehicle availability, and downtime windows.
agents.boundary: Planners and safety owners approve work and mobilization.

systems.name: Asset historian
systems.role: Provides timestamped sensor observations and quality flags through a read-only analysis interface.

systems.name: Enterprise maintenance system
systems.role: Owns equipment hierarchy, work orders, inspections, and approved maintenance procedures.

systems.name: Weather and resource planning systems
systems.role: Supply forecast revisions, access constraints, crew qualifications, and spare reservations.

flow.title: Register anomaly
flow.description: Attach asset identity, sensor quality, detection interval, and existing work-order references to prevent duplicate investigations.

flow.title: Inspect condition evidence
flow.description: Compare the anomaly with operating regime and historical baseline without translating a statistical alert into a confirmed fault.

flow.title: Retrieve maintenance context
flow.description: Gather component age, recent interventions, unresolved inspections, and applicable procedure revisions.

flow.title: Evaluate feasible windows
flow.description: Apply current weather, access, crew, and parts constraints through a deterministic scheduling service with explicit forecast expiry.

flow.title: Review work package
flow.description: Present engineers with hypotheses, required inspections, mobilization dependencies, and conditions that would invalidate the plan.

flow.title: Publish approved work
flow.description: Reserve resources and create the approved work order; revalidate weather and access before mobilization through established operational procedures.

diagrams.caption: A sensor calibration fault mimics equipment degradation. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: A sensor calibration fault mimics equipment degradation.
failures.detection: Quality flags and neighboring sensor trends contradict the apparent anomaly.
failures.recovery: Route a sensor-validation task and keep equipment conclusions provisional pending engineering review.

failures.scenario: Weather conditions change after the work package is approved.
failures.detection: Forecast revision breaches the approved access window or plan expiry.
failures.recovery: Suspend mobilization and return the plan to the authorized maintenance and safety owners.

controls: Keep turbine control, protection, and market dispatch interfaces inaccessible to agents.
Use approved safety constraints from controlled procedures, never model-generated thresholds.
Attach sensor units, quality flags, and operating regime to every condition summary.
Bind work approval to equipment, procedure revision, resources, and weather assumptions.
Require current crew qualification and access authorization before mobilization.

metrics.name: Work-package preparation time
metrics.definition: Elapsed time from accepted anomaly to engineer-reviewable maintenance scope.

metrics.name: Evidence sufficiency
metrics.definition: Work packages containing required sensor, history, and procedure references divided by reviewed packages.

metrics.name: Window invalidation rate
metrics.definition: Approved plans suspended by changed access conditions divided by approved plans.

metrics.name: Resource reservation waste
metrics.definition: Expired or cancelled reservations that were not released within the operational deadline.

tradeoffs.cost: Frequent forecast updates can require repeated review.

tradeoffs.benefit: Connects sensor alerts to asset history.
tradeoffs.cost: Data quality and operating-regime differences complicate interpretation.

tradeoffs.benefit: Prevents planning assistants from changing live equipment.
tradeoffs.cost: Execution still depends on established control-room and field procedures.

rollout.acceptance: Engineers verify evidence summaries and distinguish sensor faults from confirmed equipment findings.
One asset group compares draft packages with planner work and validates access-constraint enforcement.
Resource reservations launch after weather-change, duplicate-anomaly, and qualification-expiry tests pass.
